- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is trending up, lower the forecast by 3–7% to reflect bearish sentiment bias.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive drops), adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to avoid lagged overcorrection.  
- If forecast overshoots true outcome by >10% in early days (e.g., day 1–5), apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating ±0.3) and forecast is erratic, use a smoothing filter: average last 3–5 forecast values before final output.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the first 5–7 days of forecast are significantly higher than true outcome, apply a “downward bias” correction: subtract 2–5% from early forecast values.  
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.2) and forecast is trending up, treat as “false breakout” — reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid sentiment misalignment.
